messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED · High CPU OOMs observed on preprocessor pods in us-west-2 starting 1860004310. PagerDuty: PD#12345 paging sre-oncall and runtime-eng :rotating_light:

service-reliability: seeing repeated OOMKills on preproc-*/v1 - pods restart loop. Node pressure also reported, ~3 nodes showing >90% CPU and kernel OOM events.

sre-oncall: taking this. paging runtime-eng and ml-infra. Quick triage: are any deploys in last 30m? @eng-ops

eng-ops: no deploys in last 45m. Autoscaler did add one node at 1860004250 but pods still thrashing.

runtime-eng: logs show tokenizer worker threads spinning on a handful of very large requests. Sample log: ```2026-06-12T18:45:12Z preproc ERROR tokenizer.cpp:421 out_of_memory: requested 512MB, available 64MB -> OOMKilled```

ml-infra: looks like some prompts include huge embedded base64 sections that blow up the tokenizer buffer. We're seeing size distribution tail spike 10x normal. Also the new chunking change from last week raises per-request concurrency.

dave: confirmed customer-facing 503 spike (ingress) — synthetic monitors failing for 6 customers. CAUSE = preproc pod restarts -> request timeouts.

customer-ops: impacted customers list (from logs): cust-acme, cust-zen, cust-bolt. Notified CSMs, triage page opened.

erin: recommend immediate mitigation: 1) scale preproc replica set to +50% capacity, 2) apply emergency rate-limit by route for large payloads, 3) revert chunking concurrency env override. Who can run those?

frank: I can patch the k8s HPA and the configmap. Pushing scaled replicas now: `kubectl scale deploy preproc --replicas=18 -n inference` -> in progress.

runtime-eng: temp config to limit tokenizer concurrency: setting `MAX_TOKENIZER_THREADS=2` on preproc pods via rolling update. Will also add `TOKEN_PAYLOAD_MAX_BYTES=200000` to reject huge payloads with 413.

ml-infra: adding a defensive pre-check in the request path to reject base64 blobs > 150k and normalize long-lines. Will post PR but not safe to ship now; do emergency config first.

service-reliability: node-level mitigation: cordon node-17 and node-19 showing kernel OOMs, drain non-critical pods. `kubectl cordon node-17 && kubectl drain node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

incident-bot: ACTIONS LOGGED: scale preproc -> 18 replicas; set MAX_TOKENIZER_THREADS=2; set TOKEN_PAYLOAD_MAX_BYTES=200000; cordon/drain node-17, node-19.

dave: after scaling and thread limit, CPU util dropped to ~70% on preproc pods. Pod restart rate decreased dramatically. Latency improving. 503s dropped from 8% -> 1.2% in last 7 minutes.

erin: good. still seeing a few OOMKills on older nodes (kernel-level). Are we hitting cluster-level resource fragmentation?

runtime-eng: yes, fragmentation and high memory request pods prevented kube-scheduler packing. We should temporarily bump node pool by 3 medium instances to give headroom. Requesting eng-ops to spin up nodes.

eng-ops: spinning up 3 x c6i.large equivalents in us-west-2-nodepool-emergency. Estimated 4m until ready.

ml-infra: added quick hotfix to tokenizer to avoid preallocating giant contiguous vectors for long lines. Patch landed to hotfix branch but not rolled to production yet. We can include in a canary to one replica if safer.

frank: deployed config changes; rolling update completed at 1860005980. Replica increase done 1860005965. Node cordons done 1860005992.

service-reliability: canary shows no OOMs on that pod. Metrics stable. We should keep thread limits and payload caps for 24h and monitor.

customer-ops: sent interim status to impacted customers at 1860006000: short blip, mitigation applied, next update in 1h. No data exfiltration; requests were timing out only.

dave: quick postmortem items: 1) improve large payload detection in edge; 2) add early tokenizer backpressure; 3) add a circuit-breaker on per-customer payload concurrency; 4) test tokenization memory usage with synthetic giant-lines.

sre-oncall: handing off to night oncall. Summary: CPU OOM from tokenizer spikes due to large payloads + recent chunking concurrency increase. Immediate mitigations: scaled replicas, reduced tokenizer threads, payload max cap, cordoned flapping nodes, spun up extra nodes, hotfix prepared. Customer impact minimal after mitigations (peak 8% 503, now 0.8-1.5%).

sre-oncall: @oncall-night please take over. Handoff notes: keep MAX_TOKENIZER_THREADS=2, don't roll chunking concurrency change until we validate hotfix on canary. Watch pod restart count and node kernel OOM alerts. PD#12345 will stay active.

incident-bot: HANDOFF created -> oncall-night assigned. Timeline saved to incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incidents/PD-12345

oncall-night: ack. Will monitor and escalate if restarts >3/hr or customer error >2%.

frank: follow-up: opened GH issue ml-infra#789 for tokenizer mem-safety; PR for hotfix is #790. Scheduling canary rollout tomorrow 02:00 UTC after QA.

service-reliability: closing this thread when metrics stable for 2h. Current status: mitigated. :white_check_mark:
